parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why the partners were not sure of the value of the goodwill.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
State which partner would prefer the value given to the goodwill to be as low as possible.
Give a reason for your answer.
Partner ______
Reason ______

Additional information
The partners finally agreed on a value of $100 000 for the goodwill and the capital accounts were
adjusted.
Later that year Andy decided that he no longer wanted to work the extra hours, and the partners
decided to sell the business.
The business was acquired by AD plc on 31 December 2023. It took over all the assets and
liabilities of the partnership except for the bank account for a purchase consideration of $620 000.
The partnership’s statement of financial position immediately prior to the acquisition showed the
following:
Andy’s capital and current accounts 221 500
Betty’s capital and current accounts 291 300
Bank 49 900 debit
The partnership also paid legal fees of $3000 in relation to the sale of the business.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the profit on realisation made by the partnership.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss how Betty’s decision to agree to Andy’s suggestion to change the partnership
agreement impacted Betty. Support your answer with calculations.

Additional information
The purchase consideration was settled by $200 000 in cash and 600 000 ordinary shares of
$0.50 each.
Assets and liabilities were taken over at the following values.
Premises 510 000
Fixtures 18 000
Inventory 42 200
Trade payables 15 600

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Prepare the journal entry in the books of AD plc to record the acquisition of the partnership.
A narrative is required.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text: Advise Betty whether she should keep her shares in AD plc or sell them. Justify your answer.

Advise the managing committee whether or not they should start to include the value of the
inventory of refreshments and refuse bags in the financial statements. Justify your answer.

Additional information
Members wear coloured jackets belonging to C Society whilst on the beaches. Every year four or
five jackets go missing and have to be replaced. In 2023 four new jackets were purchased.
A local pharmaceutical company with a factory on the coast nearby has made a cash donation of
$400 to C Society every year since it started. It has now suggested that it stops making the cash
donation and instead provides C Society with nine new jackets each year. These would bear a
large logo of the pharmaceutical company across the back.

parts.label: (f)
